subject: Re: Follow-up: FinWave discovery — model fit, quantization tradeoffs, next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Soto <alex.soto@finwave.ai>
Cc: Priya Menon <p.menon@finwave.ai>
Date: 2026-03-15T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: FinWave discovery — model fit, quantization tradeoffs, next steps

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for the call today — great to meet the FinWave team. Quick recap and recommended next steps so we have aligned expectations: 

Call recap:
- Goal: Reduce model inference cost by ~3x for daily summarization + Q&A while keeping accuracy/hallucination risk within current bounds.
- Current setup: in-house LLM-based summarization pipeline (hybrid prompt) with tight accuracy requirements for financial data.
- Primary constraints: maintain high factuality on numeric data, target median latency 300–500 ms/query, and reduce per-token cost.

What we recommend as the next steps (proposed):
1) Share a representative prompt set and 50–200 sample inputs (anonymized) — that will let us run head-to-head evals.
2) Redwood will run a model-fit & quantization trade study (AWQ vs GPTQ vs FP8) on two candidate models and provide a quality/latency/cost matrix.
3) We’ll include suggested quantization profiles (AWQ-4, GPTQ-4, FP8 baseline) and run embed-similarity, ROUGE-style metrics, plus a hallucination checklist.
4) Recommend an internal POC timeline: 3–5 business days for initial trade study; 1–2 weeks for expanded evals.

Questions for you:
- Can you share the prompt set and three examples we should prioritize? (I attached a prompt template if useful.)
- Are there any regulatory/data retention constraints we should be aware of for eval data?
- Target throughput vs latency tradeoff preference (lower cost or lower latency if we must prioritize one)?

Attachments: finwave_promptset_v1.csv (prompt template), finwave_stack_diagram.png (high level). I also attached a short AWQ/GPTQ/FP8 tradeoffs primer for context.

If that sounds good I’ll kick off the eval and loop in Rishi + Dev to scope the tests.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.inference
(415) 555-0142

From: Alex Soto <alex.soto@finwave.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Cc: Priya Menon <p.menon@finwave.ai>
Date: 2026-03-15T17:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: FinWave discovery — model fit, quantization tradeoffs, next steps

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear next steps. We attached the anonymized prompt set and a few example outputs from our current pipeline. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Our primary blocker is cost: we saw token pricing balloon on peak days. We’d like to reduce run cost significantly (target ~3x reduction) but can’t accept >3% drop in accuracy on the numeric extraction/summarization bench you mentioned.
- We’re particularly worried about quantization-induced number hallucinations (e.g., rounding or swapped digits).
- On hardware: we mostly run on cloud VMs with A100 or H100 depending on the day; we can also run a short test on a single on-prem 80GB A100 if needed.

Please run the trade study focused on: Llama-2-Chat-70B and Mistral-40B-Instruct (or similar), and include AWQ vs GPTQ vs FP8 across those models. We’ll also share a short list of high-sensitivity prompts to treat as blockers.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Soto
Head of ML Engineering | FinWave
alex.soto@finwave.ai

Attachments: finwave_prompt_samples_anonymized.csv

Subject: Fwd: FinWave — request: quantization tradeoffs + eval plan

FYI — Alex from FinWave confirmed and attached the prompt set. They want a focused AWQ vs GPTQ vs FP8 trade study across two models (Llama-2-Chat-70B and Mistral-40B-Instruct). Their priorities: avoid numeric hallucinations, meet ~300–500ms median latency, and ~3x cost reduction target.

Requested from eng:
- Quick plan for bench: which infra we should run on (A100 / H100), recommended baseline (FP16), and quantization configs to test (AWQ-4, GPTQ-4, FP8/FP16).
- Define quality metrics (embed-sim, ROUGE/recall for extraction, hallucination checklist) and how we’ll capture regression.
- Estimate time & artifacts: expected token throughput, cost delta estimates, and a short report + drive link.

Attachments forwarded: finwave_promptset_v1.csv, awq_gptq_fp8_tradeoffs.pdf

If you can scope this today I’ll share timeline back to Alex; they’re ready to move quickly.

—Marissa
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, dev_patel <dev@redwood.inference>, monica_patel <monica@redwood.inference>
Cc: Alex Soto <alex.soto@finwave.ai>
Date: 2026-03-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: FinWave — request: quantization tradeoffs + eval plan

Thanks Marissa — plan below. I’ll own the initial trade study and can turn around an exec-friendly matrix in 3 business days once the prompt set is in S3/Drive. We’ll include raw artifacts (samples, metrics, and small playback harness).

High-level approach:
1) Baseline setup: FP16 runs on Llama-2-Chat-70B and Mistral-40B-Instruct to capture gold outputs (latency, token cost, and quality).
2) Quantization configs to test (parallel runs):
   - AWQ-4 (KV-cache preserved where applicable)
   - GPTQ-4 (standard GPTQ pipeline)
   - FP8 (experimental, best on H100; use for throughput ceiling)
3) Metrics we’ll report:
   - Latency (p50/p95), tokens/sec, and per-request cost estimate (rough $/1k tokens)
   - Quality: embed-similarity (sentence-transformers), ROUGE-L for summarization, exact-match on numeric extraction, and hallucination-rate checklist (manual spot checks + automated heuristics)
   - Regression signal: delta vs FP16 baseline (absolute and relative) and flagged blockers (any numeric extraction drop >1% will be highlighted)
4) Run infra: prioritize H100 for FP8 and A100 for AWQ/GPTQ comparisons. If FinWave can give us a one-off A100-80GB instance we’ll reproduce their environment.
5) Deliverables / timeline:
   - Day 0: prompt set + sensitive prompt list loaded to eval Drive (link below).
   - Day 1–2: run baseline & quantized runs (parallel).
   - Day 3: collate metrics, create short tradeoff matrix + recommended quantization profile per model.

Initial recommendations (quick take):
- Llama-2-Chat-70B + AWQ-4 often gives best cost/quality balance on instruction workloads; watch numeric extraction closely and add per-prompt canonicalization steps.
- GPTQ-4 can be competitive after careful re-tuning but may need extra calibration for numeric fidelity.
- FP8 gives the highest throughput but is riskier for precision-sensitive prompts (useful as an upper-bound if FinWave wants to prioritize cost/throughput and accept higher QA gating).

Next steps: I’ll provision jobs and post results to the Drive link below:
- https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/finwave/evals/finwave_prompts_v1
- HubSpot: HS-123456

I’ll also attach the raw run configs and a small eval harness we can hand over. If Alex wants, we can schedule a follow-up to walk through the matrix after Day 3.

—Rishi
Director, Applied ML | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.inference
